title: The EIFFEL TOWER Gets Taller in Summer 🗼
description:
Hold up your phone: in summer, the Eiffel Tower can grow about that much! Hot iron stretches, like a cat in a sunbeam. The tower is about 18,000 iron pieces, and in the heat each one gets a hair longer. Stack it all up: up to about 15 cm, one phone. And on sunny days the sunny side stretches more than the shady side, so the top leans AWAY from the Sun.
Summer or winter: when would you visit?

The science: iron expands as it warms. The tower's puddled iron grows by about 12 millionths of its length for every degree Celsius, so its 300 metres of iron gain roughly 3.6 mm per degree, several centimetres between a freezing winter day and a hot summer afternoon. A physicist writing in The Conversation puts the real seasonal change at about 12 to 15 cm; the tower's own website describes it more modestly as a few millimetres to centimetres of height, so take 15 cm as the top of the range. The tower's operator also explains that the Sun heats one face at a time, so on a clear day the top moves along a curve about 15 cm across, leaning away from the Sun (the animation exaggerates it about 100 times so you can see it). The tower has 18,038 metal pieces held by about 2.5 million rivets.
